1  2  2025:KER:1980  JUDGMENT Dated this the 8th day of January, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.)No.870/2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda is the appellant herein.

The respondents in the O.P.
are the respondents herein.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 2.2.2011.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal.

2. According to the petitioner, on 2.2.2011 at about 6.45 p.m., while he was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No. KL-8-Z-4319, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-47-7897 ridden by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on his motorcycle.
As a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
The 1 st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the rider and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to him, the accident occurred due to 2025:KER:1980 the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.1,50,000/-.
3. The 1st and 2nd respondents remained ex-parte.
The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and further contending that the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
It is also alleged that the 2nd respondent had no valid driving licence and hence the 3 rd respondent had no responsibility to indemnify the 1st respondent.
4. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of Pws1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exhibits A1 to A9, B1 and B2.
5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.86,250/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

sentences.text:
Heard Smt. Jeena Joseph, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri.P.K. Babu,
learned Standing Counsel for the respondent.
9. The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
Though in the written statement the 3 rd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner, it was found against by the Tribunal.
The said finding remains unchallenged.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.
10. The petitioner was aged 22 years on the date of the accident, on 2.2.2011
According to the petitioner, he was a driver by profession, earning Rs. 6,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed his income at Rs.4,000/-.

Since he could not prove the income claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], his notional income is liable 2025:KER:1980 to be fixed at Rs.8,000/-.
11.

sentences.text: The petitioner produced per Ext.A5 disability certificate issued by PW2, Doctor, showing that he has a permanent disability of 9%.
The Doctor who examined the petitioner and issued Exhibit A5 was also examined before the Tribunal.
Even then, the Tribunal has fixed his disability at 5%.

As per Exhibit A5 disability certificate issued by PW2, the Doctor, the petitioner has difficulties of post traumatic osteoarthritis and partial ankylosis of (right) knee joint, Grade 4 muscle strength of right quadriceps muscle and implant in situ which requires another surgery for removal.
For the reason that the petitioner was not examined by the Medical Board, the disability assessed by PW2 was not accepted as such by the Tribunal.

Since from the evidence of PW2, the Doctor who issued Exhibit A5, it is revealed that the petitioner sustained post traumatic osteoarthritis and partial ankylosis of (right) knee joint, Grade 4 muscle strength of right quadriceps muscle and implant in situ which requires another surgery for removal, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the evidence of PW2 that the petitioner has a disability of 9%.
Therefore, the disability of the petitioner is accepted as 9%.

Since, on the date of accident, he was aged 22 years, 50% of his income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].
13.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.2,33,280/-.
14.Towards loss of earnings the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.12,000/- being 3 months income.
Since his notional income is enhanced to Rs.8,000/-, the petitioner is entitled to get Rs.24,000/- on that head.

sentences.text: 15. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,000/-.

Considering the fact that in the accident the petitioner sustained fracture of shaft of right femur in addition to other injuries and he sustained 9% disability, the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lesser side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.

16. Towards the head compensation for loss of amenities, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/-,
which according to the learned counsel 2025:KER:1980 for the petitioner, is on the lower side.
The petitioner was treated as an inpatient for 10 days.
Because of the injuries sustained by him, he had to take rest for a period of 3 months.
In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards loss of amenities is on the lesser side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
17. Towards extra nourishment, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.1,000/-, which, according to the petitioner is also on the lesser side.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the percentage of disability suffered by him the compensation awarded for extra nourishment is on the lesser side, and hence it is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.3,57,330/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

Sl . Head of claim Amount awarded by Amount No. the Tribunal (Rs)
modified in appeal (Rs.) 1 Loss of earning 12,000/- 24,000/-
2
Transportation charges 1,000/- 1,000/- 3 Extra nourishment 1,000/- 10,000/- 4 Damage to clothing & articles 500/- 500/- 5
Bystander's expenses 1,000/- 1,000/- 6
Medical expenses 12,550/- 12,550/- 7 Pain and suffering 10,000/- 50,000/- 8
Permanent disability 43,200/- 2,33,280/- 9 Loss of amenities 5,000/- 25,000/-

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.3,57,330/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Fifty Seven Thousand Three Hundred and Thirty Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
